what_happened: Mechanically reproduced the cited BimodalLogic:#833 incident by running the CURRENT plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, with PLAN_FILE_SCOPE_HARVEST_ROOT pointed at the real (read-only) BimodalLogic checkout, against the actual archived plan file for task 833. The harvester correctly appended both typst/generated/status.typ and the repository-root README.md to the harvested set -- exactly the two surfaces the incident reports as missed. Cross-checked against BimodalLogic's own specs/archive/state.json file_scope for task 833, which already lists both surfaces. This falsifies both of part (1)'s offered hypotheses (no .lean path harvested; ancestor-chain walk missing the root) and localizes the real gap to a pipeline-visibility issue outside the two files this task's file_scope declares.

The dispatch's own premise (determine why generated-surface appending did not cover the cited case) is refuted for the appending mechanism itself: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh already computes and persists the correct file_scope (verified by reproduction). The actual gap: the appended surfaces land only in state.json file_scope -- never written back into the plan document's own per-phase Files-to-modify prose (the harvester only reads the plan, never writes it), and never read by orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh when building an implement dispatch (file_scope appears there only in a sibling-batch-overlap comment). The implementing agent has zero visibility into the correctly-computed surfaces at the point it matters. A fix belongs in the dispatch-construction/plan-postflight pipeline, not in the two files this task declares.

Plan-time premise re-validation reproduced the research figure exactly rather than carrying it: the harvester run against the consumer repository's archived plan emitted a byte-identical 7-path array including typst/generated/status.typ and the root README.md, and the root marker is still the plain dir=FormalSystem form at README.md:19. The reproduction is cheap and repeatable, so the plan makes it a go/no-go Phase 1 instead of a trusted figure.

Plan-time refinement of the research finding: the research report located two blind channels for a correctly-computed generated-surface append (the plan document's own per-phase prose, and the implement-dispatch prompt). The first is in fact already covered at the authoring layer by plan-format.md's coupled-generated-surface declaration obligation, which landed after the cited incident, so the planner now owes the derived-surface declaration in the phase that moves its input. Only the dispatch-prompt channel remains blind (grep -c file_scope against orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh still returns 1, a sibling-batch comment). This narrows the residual follow-up recommendation and is recorded in the plan's header-record phase rather than widened into this record's scope.

Phase 1 re-validation at implementation time agrees exactly with the plan-time figures: the real-incident reproduction against the live BimodalLogic checkout (PLAN_FILE_SCOPE_HARVEST_ROOT=/home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic against specs/archive/833_stab_definable_from_open_modals/plans/01_stab-definable-from-open-modals.md) emits the byte-identical 7-entry array including both typst/generated/status.typ and the bare README.md; the root README.md marker is confirmed as 'dir=FormalSystem rows=totals desc=no'; orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh still shows exactly one file_scope hit (a sibling-batch comment, not a read of the dispatching task's own file_scope); and the suite's highest existing case number is confirmed as 29, so the new fixture case in Phase 2 is Case 30. No disagreement found; proceeding to Phase 2 as planned.
